decisions.summary: Separate statutory and internal-policy rule bases
decisions.concern: Internal policy is stricter than Article 50 for deployers (e.g. notices for direct interaction).
options: Keep one row per system per rule basis
decisions.source_basis: Interview 03:24 PM ('use the binding Article 50 text and the internal policy to evaluate our controls'); policy approval boundary.
decisions.chosen_behavior: Each register row has rule_ref and rule_basis; statutory rows go to Legal, policy rows to Operations.
decisions.rationale: Legal and Operations own different decisions; mixing bases would misstate legal exposure.
tradeoffs: More rows for reviewers to read
decisions.downstream_effect: Approval requirements are routed by rule basis.

decisions.summary: Quillhaven's role is taken from the register and corroborated by the policy operating facts
decisions.concern: Provider duties (50(1), 50(2)) and deployer duties (50(3), 50(4)) differ.
options: Use register role, corroborate with the policy context, unresolved when either is open
decisions.chosen_behavior: Deployer-only when both agree; unknown (AI-005) stays unresolved with the owner's refresh as the need.
decisions.rationale: Role decides which paragraph applies; it must not be assumed.
tradeoffs: Conclusions for supplier products depend on owner-supplied facts that the policy says are not Legal decisions
decisions.downstream_effect: Statutory no-impact rows explain that provider duties sit with the supplier and ask Legal to confirm.
